articles.title: NASA, Partners Accelerate Lander Development for 2028 Moon Missions
articles.description: As NASA returns humans to the lunar surface and establishes a long-term presence on our closest celestial neighbor, the agency and commercial human landing system providers Blue Origin and SpaceX have streamlined the designs and changed both concepts of operations for its future crewed landers. Since NASA established initial contracts with Blue Origin and SpaceX […]
articles.summary: NASA and partners accelerate development of advanced landers for 2028 Moon missions as humanity prepares to return to the lunar surface. This marks a major milestone in establishing sustained human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis III Mission to Test Future Moon Lander Operations
articles.description: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history.  Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit […]
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis III mission will conduct groundbreaking tests of next-generation Moon lander operations before astronauts return to the lunar surface. A pivotal step in advancing human spaceflight capabilities.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully launches toward Phobos, marking an exciting step in exploring the Martian system. This ambitious mission will study Mars's mysterious moons and return samples to Earth.

articles.title: NASA adopting Apollo's urgency to build a moon base and land astronauts within 2 years
articles.description: NASA is moving fast on its plans to build a moon base and return astronauts to the lunar surface in as little as two years.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA accelerates its lunar ambitions by adopting Apollo-era urgency to establish a moon base and return astronauts within two years.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples from asteroid Bennu reveal 4.5-billion-year-old secrets about our Solar System's formation, fundamentally reshaping our understanding of planetary origins.

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
articles.summary: Analysis of 2,884 exploding stars provides groundbreaking new evidence about dark energy and the Universe's expansion, challenging current cosmological models.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
articles.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.
articles.summary: Scientists achieved a major breakthrough measuring conditions during the Universe's first five minutes, unlocking secrets of the earliest cosmic moments.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Astronomers confirm the first microblazar discovery, a groundbreaking finding that expands our understanding of high-energy cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: NASA’s Swift Mission Ends, Leaves Behind Scientific Bonanza
articles.description: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has ended its science mission now that the spacecraft is orbiting less than 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth’s surface. The greater atmospheric drag at this height prevents the satellite’s telescopes from steadily gazing at their astronomical targets. Swift conducted its final observation on Oct. 20. It is expected to […]
articles.summary: NASA's Swift Observatory concludes its mission after years of groundbreaking observations, leaving behind a remarkable scientific legacy. The telescope revolutionized our understanding of gamma-ray bursts and cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description:
Image:
			Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.summary: Stunning imagery captures the dynamic process of star formation within a luminous nebula. A celestial cauldron where gravity and stellar nurseries create the next generation of stars.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates eight years of successful operation studying Mercury with groundbreaking observations. The ESA-JAXA collaboration continues to unlock the secrets of the solar system's innermost planet.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: ESA's Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exceptional observational capabilities. A remarkable achievement in expanding our catalog of solar system objects.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launches on October 19 to explore the Martian moons and advance our understanding of Mars. An important international effort to study the Red Planet's mysterious satellites.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter spacecraft investigates mysterious magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, revealing new insights into the Sun's magnetic behavior. Groundbreaking observations advance our understanding of solar physics and space weather.

articles.title: 27 Exoplanet Targets for the World's First Private Space Telescope
articles.description: Get ready for the age of private space telescopes. The Lazuli Space Telescope will launch in a few years and part of its mission is to observe exoplanets. New research presents a list of 27 exoplanet targets, some of which are very well-known and will certainly benefit from deeper observations.
articles.summary: The Lazuli Space Telescope, the first private space telescope, will launch in the coming years and target 27 exoplanets for groundbreaking observations.

articles.title: JWST Reveals a Lopsided Alien World with Blistering Evening Winds
articles.description: Typically, when we think of exoplanets, we think of neat spheres floating directly in front of their star, which acts as a giant spotlight. From our vantage point, they would look more like two perfect two dimensional circles than spheres, though. But nature is almost never so clean-cut. A new paper published in Nature Astronomy from researchers at Cornell and the University of Bristol details the first-ever study of an exoplanet that is noticeably lopsided.
articles.summary: JWST reveals an asymmetrical exoplanet with extreme dayside winds, challenging conventional models of alien world atmospheres.

articles.title: Even the Rubin's Test Camera Produces Stunning Images
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory's Commissioning Camera operated for about 7 weeks in 2024, before the observatory released its well-known first look images. It's an engineering camera, and its job was to test the VRO's equipment and procedures. Now, the VRO has released the ComCam's image of the Seagull nebula. It's a pretty stunning image for an engineering camera.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory's test camera produces spectacular images during commissioning, promising remarkable discoveries ahead.

articles.title: Black holes spinning near maximum rate could split in two, calculations suggest
articles.description: Two black holes can collide and merge into one. But could the opposite happen: could a single black hole split into two smaller ones? That question is explored in a new theoretical study: "When Black Holes Admit Pair-of-pants Topologies," published in the journal Physical Review D.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Theoretical calculations suggest that rapidly spinning black holes near their maximum rotation rate could potentially split apart into two separate black holes.

articles.title: ALMA spots 'dragon egg' that may represent the earliest stages of massive star formation
articles.description: Astronomers identified an exceptionally tiny core that may represent an early stage in the formation of a massive star. Located in an infrared-dark area called Dragon Cloud, the core is nicknamed the "dragon egg." The paper, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics, was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 5.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: ALMA discovers a 'dragon egg' core that may represent the earliest observable stage of massive star formation in the universe.

articles.title: Artemis I: Crystals of experimental detectors record radiation doses near the moon
articles.description: Do cosmic radiation doses near the moon differ significantly from those received by astronauts in low Earth orbit? Experimental lithium fluoride detectors, installed aboard the Orion spacecraft during the Artemis I mission, have now made it possible to obtain preliminary estimates.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Artemis I's experimental detectors measured cosmic radiation doses near the Moon, providing crucial data on radiation exposure for future lunar missions compared to low Earth orbit levels.

articles.title: Pedal to the metal: NASA's Psyche heads toward asteroid belt
articles.description: With a successful Mars gravity assist in its rearview mirror, NASA's Psyche spacecraft has fired up its thrusters and is accelerating toward the metal-rich asteroid of the same name. During the first leg of its journey, following an October 2023 launch, the mission used its electric propulsion system intermittently to maneuver into the right position to harness Mars' gravity for a propellant-saving speed boost and a slight trajectory change.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's Psyche spacecraft successfully completed a Mars gravity assist and is now accelerating toward the asteroid belt to study a unique metal-rich asteroid.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
articles.description: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a surprisingly complex magnetic web above the Sun using advanced balloon-borne telescopes, revealing hidden structures in the Sun's quiet regions.

articles.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
articles.description: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight. Researchers found that astronauts' hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and handled simulated Martian gravity without major problems, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.
articles.summary: A study of 13 astronauts shows the human heart may be surprisingly resilient for Mars missions, offering encouraging news for future deep space exploration.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover just shattered the all-time off-world driving record
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has shattered a historic space exploration record, traveling farther across another world than any vehicle before it. Its advanced self-driving system helped it surpass Opportunity’s 28.06-mile record in just five and a half years, a feat that previously took nearly 15. Now, Perseverance is exploring some of the oldest rocks in the solar system, searching for clues about ancient Martian environments that may once have supported life.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover shattered the all-time off-world driving record, continuing its historic exploration of the Martian surface.

articles.title: NASA lays out plan for Artemis 3 moon-lander test flight —but when will it launch?
articles.description: NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight, which is scheduled to launch to Earth orbit next year. But a firm liftoff date has not yet been announced.
articles.summary: NASA reveals detailed plans for its Artemis III moon-lander test flight, marking a major milestone in humanity's return to the lunar surface.

articles.title: Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? [8:42]
articles.description: A leading theory proposes that ancient Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? | 8:42 VideoFr…
articles.summary: Exploring the leading Giant Impact Hypothesis theory that a planet-sized collision with ancient Earth created our moon, a transformative moment in solar system history.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA JPL envisions 90 years of future innovation including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Martian helicopters, inspiring the next generation of space exploration.

articles.title: SpaceX показала интерьер Starship для NASA: деревянный потолок и минимализм для полетов на Луну
articles.description: SpaceX показала, как будет выглядеть жилой отсек Starship для будущих высадок астронавтов NASA на Луну.
articles.summary: SpaceX reveals the interior design of Starship's crew habitat for NASA lunar missions, showcasing innovative minimalist design for future astronaut expeditions.

articles.title: En étudiant Saturne, des astronomes découvrent un étrange décagone géant autour de son pôle sud
articles.description:
L’examen des clichés du télescope spatial Hubble a révélé une nouvelle « bizarrerie » dans l’atmosphère de Saturne, dont les mécanismes de formation restent à ce stade mal compris.
The post En étudiant Saturne, des astronomes découvrent un étrange décagone gé…
articles.summary: Hubble Space Telescope observations reveal a mysterious giant decagonal atmospheric feature around Saturn's south pole, adding to the planet's fascinating atmospheric phenomena.

articles.title: NASA's Perseverance Just Broke The Off-World Driving Record, While Mostly Steering Itself
articles.description: When we look up at Mars, many millions of miles away, it's inspiring to think that someone may be looking back at us – not any heat-ray-equipped aliens, thankfully, but one of humanity's greatest accomplishments: NASA's Perseverance rover.  In July of 2020, t…
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover sets a new off-world driving record on Mars while demonstrating impressive autonomous navigation capabilities.
